content:
ale: Noticed a weird failure in the sample-app onboarding flow when built with webpack 5 + terser: auth.retry wrapper disappears and TypeScript typings don't match at runtime.

ale: Quick summary: sample-app imports SDK like `import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` (TS, esModuleInterop false). Works in node ESM but when we ship a browser bundle (webpack -> terser) or Vite SSR build, client.auth is undefined in some consumers.

ale: Repro (webpack):
```js
// src/entry.ts
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.auth.getToken(); // throws because auth is undefined
```

ale: Repro steps:
1. clone minimal sample-app
2. npm i && npm run build:web (webpack config: target: web, mode: production, optimization: { minimize: true })
3. Serve dist and open login flow -> runtime: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getToken')`

tim: I reproduced locally. Vite SSR produces slightly different shape: auth exists but client.auth.retry is undefined. Looks like our helpers are attached via side-effect function calls that some bundlers treeshake because they think the export isn't used. Terser mangling + property renaming also made the wrapper name mismatch in one case.

yara: This smells like two separate issues: 1) side-effect attachers being tree-shaken if not referenced directly, 2) build-time minifiers renaming properties so runtime checks fail. Could also be opt-in pure annotations in our ESM build.

ale: Minimal manifest to reproduce with Vite SSR included in gist. Vite command: `vite build --ssr src/entry.ts` then `node dist/server/entry.js` -> inconsistent behavior between node vs browser bundle.

lee: Workarounds for affected customers: 
- Use import syntax and keep esModuleInterop=false or set allowSyntheticDefaultImports=true in TS.
- Disable aggressive minify / property mangling (Terser option: keep_fnames/keep_classnames and mangle: { properties: false }).
- For Vite: set build.rollupOptions.treeshake = false for a quick check.

yara: Long-term fix candidates:
- Provide explicit named exports for the auth/retry helpers so bundlers see symbol usage instead of relying on side-effect mutations.
- Ship a small browser-friendly shim that re-exports runtime shape with side-effects preserved (`dist/browser.cjs.js` + `dist/browser.esm.js`).
- Add a bundler integration test matrix: webpack-prod+terser, vite-ssr, rollup-cjs to CI.

ale: Typing pain: some sample apps using `import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` have TS inference returning `any` for client.auth because our d.ts uses `export default class RedwoodClient {}` but also attaches helpers later. We should add declarations for the runtime-augmented properties (auth, retry) on the client interface so TS picks them up.

tim: Agreed. Action items: 
- Add explicit named export `export const attachRuntimeHelpers = ...` and call it in both ESM and CJS shims to guarantee the helpers are present.
- Update types: augment RedwoodClient interface with `auth: { getToken(...): Promise<string>, retry: (fn: Function)=>Function }` (or better shapes).
- Add CI bundler tests (see yara's matrix).

dev-bot: Created issue #2892: "bundlers: ensure auth/retry not tree-shaken or mangled in production builds" assigned to eng-devex and eng-runtime.

yara: I'll prototype a shim that explicitly references the helper functions (so they are not tree-shaken) and add a webpack-prod regression test that builds the published package and a tiny consumer. If that looks stable, we can backport to the last two releases (customers hit this in sample-app v0.3.1).

lee: For docs/onboarding: add a short "Bundlers & runtime quirks" section in DX guide listing the known runtime shapes and simple quick fixes (tsconfig flags, require/import patterns, minifier flags).

ale: Also call out Cloudflare Workers and Edge SSR — they use esbuild and have different tree-shake heuristics; we saw one customer where auth was present in node but missing in their edge deployment.

yara: I'll link example webpack config & terser settings in the PR.

ale: Thanks — short-term: write doc note + quick workaround. Medium-term: export shims + type fixes + CI tests.

tim: Filed a follow-up to track backport in the releases board.

ale: Good catch everyone. I'll add the sample-app repro link to the issue and ping customers impacted. :white_check_mark:
